mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off reaction that compresses equity discounting, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such events are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS moves back below the trigger threshold within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below its 200-day moving average, it signals a shift to accommodative policy, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: transition from tightening to accommodative policy
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically higher than the pre-trigger mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market that elevates inflation expectations and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev_month PAYEMS by > 2% AND UNRATE < prev_month UNRATE by > 0.2 percentage points
regime_hint: labor market tightening before wage growth acceleration
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in such events are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or wage growth (HOUST) rises > 3% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 (real GDP momentum) above the 12-month rolling average coincides with rising consumer confidence and higher retail sales (HOUST), predicting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: ΔGDPC1 > 0.5% monthly AND HOUST > prev_month HOUST by > 2%
regime_hint: early expansion phase in business cycle
failure_condition: In >70% of such events, the 20-day forward return is ≤ 0 (quantile rank < 30th).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) accompanied by a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) indicates weakening supply-side momentum, which is associated with lower corporate earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev_month INDPRO by > -2% AND RSAFS < prev_month RSAFS by > -3%
regime_hint: early signs of supply shock or demand softening
failure_condition: Over 100 such events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS rises above its 52-week moving average, it signals a structural shift toward tighter labor markets that elevates wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Across 200 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in FEDFUNDS suggests disinflation is being driven by central bank policy, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 AND FEDFUNDS <= prev_month FEDFUNDS by > 0.1 percentage points for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in such episodes are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in GDPC1 and HOUST (retail sales) exceeding 2% each, without a corresponding spike in UNRATE, signals robust demand growth that supports higher corporate earnings and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > prev_month GDPC1 by > 2% AND HOUST > prev_month HOUST by > 2% AND UNRATE < prev_month UNRATE
regime_hint: robust demand expansion absent wage moderation
failure_condition: In >80% of such events, the 20-day forward return is ≤ 0 (quantile rank < 20th).
